title: The colleague who rewrote history in every retro
situation: A senior teammate kept saying in retros that my module caused the outage, even though the incident log showed their config change.
tactic: Stopped arguing in the meeting. Started posting a two-line written recap after every incident with the timeline, ticket IDs and owners. Asked our lead to make the incident doc the single source of truth.
outcome: Two retros later the blame stopped. Nobody argues with a timestamp.

title: Manager who never says yes or no
situation: My manager let a vendor-switch decision sit for five weeks while support tickets piled up.
tactic: Wrote a one-page impact summary, got finance and support to co-sign it, then sent: 'Unless you advise otherwise by Thursday 5pm, I will start the reversible pilot with Vendor B.'
outcome: Got a reply in two hours: 'Go ahead, keep me posted.' The pilot worked.

title: Access request stuck in IT limbo
situation: Three weeks waiting for a database read-only account, with a client deadline ten days out.
tactic: Documented the ticket history, sent an impact statement to my director, then a final request to IT copying my boss with a dated, policy-compliant workaround (approved export from the BI team).
outcome: Account created the next morning. The workaround was never needed.

title: Holiday dinner debates with my brother-in-law
situation: Every family dinner turned into a politics argument that ended with someone leaving the table.
tactic: Declined the bait twice with a calm 'Let's park that one tonight', changed the ground by suggesting a walk after dinner, and agreed with my sister beforehand on a signal to redirect.
outcome: First peaceful dinner in two years. He even laughed about it.

title: Landlord ignoring a broken heater
situation: Four messages over two weeks, no response, temperatures dropping.
tactic: Switched from texts to one dated email with photos, the lease clause and a clear repair-by date, then a polite note that I would contact the local housing office if needed.

title: Competitor undercutting us on price
situation: A bigger competitor offered our top client 20% less for the same service.
tactic: Did not match the price. Interviewed the client's operations team, found they valued faster onboarding, and offered a guaranteed 5-day setup plus quarterly reviews.
outcome: Renewed for two years at the old price.

title: Salary negotiation after a promotion
situation: Promoted to team lead, but the offer was below market and HR said the band was fixed.
tactic: Gathered three market data points and a list of the lead duties I had already been doing for six months. Asked HR what flexibility existed outside base pay before naming a number.
outcome: Base stayed in band, but got a sign-on bonus and a review date in six months in writing.

title: Drafted the angry email at 11pm
situation: A client publicly criticised my team's work in a group thread.
tactic: Wrote the furious reply, moved it to drafts, slept on it, and the next morning sent three factual lines plus an offer to talk.
outcome: The client apologised on the call. The draft is still in my folder as a reminder.
